recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group wants a broader normative-strength change, such as changing the existing lowercase "must" to "SHALL" or adding a formal invariant, because that would go beyond the applied FHIR-17173 resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-17173 was a Published FHIR-core/fhir-i change request with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. It asked to clarify the apparent conflict between the create rule that a server ignores a submitted id and applying history Bundles as transactions; the final resolution was that history-bundle entries with request.method POST must use Bundle.entry.resource.id for that resource.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 14179. In git, commit 7f62d75b702eaf8411a2e9ee065322fe7f36482d, "GF#17173 - note about processing history as transaction", added the current source/http.html note requiring history Bundle POST entries to use Bundle.entry.resource.id matching Bundle.entry.response.location so references are preserved.
additional_context: publish.ini maps http.html as the current HTTP page, so source/http.html is in build scope. The current source keeps the FHIR-17173 note in the Accepting other Bundle types section immediately after the statement that history Bundles may be treated as transactions or batches. Later HTTP-page changes did not remove or contradict the note, and targeted Zulip/Confluence searches found no relevant conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was necessary because the current HTTP source already conveys the requested history Bundle POST/id rule, and duplicating it in the create section would not change implementer expectations.
